CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A thumb piano produces sound when you (1 mark)
   A. pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   B. hit it with a big stick
   C. blow into it
   D. rub its skin

2. What is charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. Black carbon left when wood is heated with little air
   B. Ground chalk
   C. A type of clay
   D. A kind of wet paint

3. Which is the beater of a drum? (1 mark)
   A. The rope
   B. The stick or hand that strikes it
   C. The skin
   D. The shell

4. On a xylophone, the short bars give (1 mark)
   A. no sound
   B. high notes
   C. low notes
   D. the loudest sound only

5. What is the correct way to catch a netball? (1 mark)
   A. With your eyes closed
   B. With one hand held stiff
   C. With your feet
   D. With two hands, giving with the ball

6. A chest pass starts with the ball held at (1 mark)
   A. chest height
   B. the ankles
   C. above the head
   D. behind the back

7. What do you add to a colour to make it lighter? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. White
   C. More of the same colour only
   D. Soil

8. A darker tone of a colour is called a (1 mark)
   A. frame
   B. tint
   C. secondary
   D. shade

9. Which statement is true? (1 mark)
   A. A crotchet is shorter than a quaver
   B. Two quavers equal one crotchet
   C. A rest is longer than a note
   D. One quaver equals two crotchets

10. What does a crotchet look like? (1 mark)
   A. A filled-in oval with a stem
   B. A zigzag
   C. A dot only
   D. An empty circle

11. How long does a crotchet rest last? (1 mark)
   A. One beat
   B. Half a beat
   C. Two beats
   D. No time

12. Why should clay models dry slowly in the shade? (1 mark)
   A. Fast drying in strong sun can crack them
   B. Shade makes them shine
   C. Shade makes them heavy
   D. Sun makes them soft

13. How many rectangular slabs of different sizes are cut in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. One
   C. Ten
   D. Three

14. Hand signs for d, r and m are shown at heights that (1 mark)
   A. go up from d to r to m
   B. stay the same
   C. are random
   D. go down from d to m

15. A coil of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a plate
   B. a hard brick
   C. a flat sheet
   D. a long thin roll like a snake

16. A sprint is (1 mark)
   A. a very long race
   B. a jump into sand
   C. a short race run at full speed
   D. a throwing event

17. If you finish a gymnastics session, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Run around wildly
   B. Push the mats
   C. Leave mats on the floor
   D. Put equipment away and cool down

18. Where should you place your hands in a crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. In your pockets
   B. On your head
   C. Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   D. In front of your face

19. Which folk songs are sung while working? (1 mark)
   A. Naming songs
   B. Marriage songs
   C. Funeral songs
   D. Work songs

20. Which of these makes a photograph too dark? (1 mark)
   A. Too much practice
   B. A clean lens
   C. Too little light
   D. A battery

21. Which is used only for taking photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Whistle
   B. Digital camera
   C. Torch
   D. Radio

22. The screen of a camera (1 mark)
   A. is the strap
   B. is the battery
   C. makes sound
   D. shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken

23. What sound do you hear if a hole is not fully covered? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing at all
   B. A clear note
   C. A squeak or weak sound
   D. A drum sound

24. Which part of the finger covers a hole? (1 mark)
   A. The fingertip edge
   B. The soft pad
   C. The knuckle
   D. The nail

25. Where should the mouthpiece rest? (1 mark)
   A. Behind your ear
   B. On your chin
   C. Between your teeth
   D. Between your lips, not your teeth

26. Which Kiswahili word means elephant? (1 mark)
   A. kuku
   B. nyoka
   C. tembo
   D. twiga

27. Which is a rule for animal games? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore the whistle
   B. Play without looking
   C. Do not push, trip or pull others
   D. Push others to go faster

28. How many verses does the Kenya National Anthem have? (1 mark)
   A. One
   B. Two
   C. Three
   D. Four

29. Every displayed work should have (1 mark)
   A. a secret code
   B. a label with the title and artist's name
   C. a price only
   D. no name

30. How can you decorate a portfolio cover? (1 mark)
   A. By tearing it
   B. By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   C. By putting sand on it
   D. By burning it

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Name the three joints of a descant recorder and state where the mouthpiece is. (3 marks)

32. Give three responsible ways of using a device for photography. (3 marks)

33. State three qualities of good feedback. (3 marks)

34. Why should we take turns and respect others' views when talking about paintings and montages? (3 marks)

35. Write rhythm patterns for the elephant walk and the hare hop using rhythm names. (3 marks)

36. Why is it important to appreciate the percussion instruments of different communities? (3 marks)

37. State what red, white and the shield stand for on the Kenyan flag. (3 marks)

38. Describe a full netball court. (3 marks)

39. Name two parts of a drum. (2 marks)

40. Explain the steps of a full sprint from the start commands to the finish. (5 marks)

41. Describe the roles in a folk song performance. (4 marks)

42. Explain how to take a portrait of a friend with good light and a clear centre of interest. (5 marks)

43. State two ways of playing percussion instruments. (2 marks)

44. Why is it important to keep the right posture during a sprint? (3 marks)

45. Give three ways of caring for a digital camera. (3 marks)

46. How should clay models be dried and why? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   The kalimba or mbira has metal tongues that you pluck with the thumbs.

2. A — Black carbon left when wood is heated with little air
   Charcoal is the black carbon left after wood is burned with very little air.

3. B — The stick or hand that strikes it
   The beater is what hits the drumhead.

4. B — high notes
   Shorter bars vibrate faster and sound higher.

5. D — With two hands, giving with the ball
   A double-handed catch with elbows bending as the ball arrives is correct.

6. A — chest height
   A chest pass begins with the ball at chest level.

7. B — White
   White makes a tint, a lighter tone.

8. D — shade
   Adding black makes a shade.

9. B — Two quavers equal one crotchet
   1/2 + 1/2 = 1 beat.

10. A — A filled-in oval with a stem
   A crotchet has a filled note head and a stem.

11. A — One beat
   A crotchet rest is one beat of silence.

12. A — Fast drying in strong sun can crack them
   Slow drying prevents cracks.

13. D — Three
   Three slabs are cut, one for each of d, r and m.

14. A — go up from d to r to m
   The signs rise as the pitch rises.

15. D — a long thin roll like a snake
   A coil is a long, thin, even roll of clay.

16. C — a short race run at full speed
   Sprints such as 50 m or 100 m are short races.

17. D — Put equipment away and cool down
   Tidying and cooling down are good habits.

18. C — Behind you, shoulder-width apart
   Hands go behind you, about shoulder-width apart.

19. D — Work songs
   Work songs give rhythm to work.

20. C — Too little light
   Poor light makes dark pictures.

21. B — Digital camera
   A digital camera is made for photography.

22. D — shows what you will photograph and photos you have taken
   The screen displays the view and the saved pictures.

23. C — A squeak or weak sound
   Leaks make squeaks.

24. B — The soft pad
   Pads seal the hole fully.

25. D — Between your lips, not your teeth
   Lips form the seal.

26. C — tembo
   Tembo is an elephant.

27. C — Do not push, trip or pull others
   Safety comes first.

28. C — Three
   The anthem has three verses.

29. B — a label with the title and artist's name
   Labels help viewers.

30. B — By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   Decorating uses local resources.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Head joint, middle joint and foot joint. The mouthpiece is on the head joint.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the joints, 1 mark for order or naming all, 1 mark for the mouthpiece.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission before photographing someone; do not photograph in private places; do not share photographs without permission; use it only for the set task. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is fair, it shows respect and it helps everyone learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Elephant walk: taa taa taa (rest). Hare hop: ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern, 1 mark for correct rest or names.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show the culture and skill of each community. They help us respect one another. They should be preserved for future generations.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Red stands for the blood shed for freedom. White stands for peace and honesty. The shield and spears stand for the defence of freedom.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a rectangle 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide. It is divided into three equal thirds. It has a goal post at each end with a goal circle and a centre circle in the middle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rectangle with measurements, 1 mark for thirds, 1 mark for circles or posts.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Drumhead (skin) and shell (body). Rope and beater are also accepted.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct part.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: On your marks: go to the line and take the position. Set: lift the hips slightly and stay still. Go: push hard and swing the arms. Run in your lane with high knees and bent arms. Keep running through the finish line and slow down gradually.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for marks, set, go, running technique and finishing.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads the song; the chorus answers or repeats; the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat; dancers move to the music.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission. Put the sun behind you so light falls on the friend's face. Choose a plain background. Move closer so the face fills the picture. Hold the device steadily, press gently and check the photograph.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Striking and shaking. Scraping is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the body moving forward in a straight line. It saves energy and helps speed. It prevents pain or injury.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold with two hands; use a strap; clean the lens with a soft dry cloth; keep away from water and dust; charge the battery. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Slowly in the shade. Strong sun dries them too fast and makes them crack.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
